correctness.rationale: For an invariant unoriented Crofton line conditioned to meet convex polygon K, total line intensity is perimeter P. The event of cap area <=epsilon*A is exactly the sum of two support-cap offset widths; angular orientation conversion yields (1/P)int_0^{2pi}delta(u,epsilon*A)du. At almost every normal exposing a vertex with interior angle alpha, the small cap triangle has area delta^2 sin(alpha)/(2pq), yielding its J(alpha) coefficient. An inscribed disk yields uniform O(sqrt(area)) domination allowing angular dominated convergence. AM-GM on incident projections and 2sqrt(ab)<=a+b give strict C<sqrt2 for parallelograms, approached by flattening rhombi. The small exterior-angle integral produces C(P_n)=pi^2/(4sqrt(n))+O(n^-5/2), distinct from the circular cap exponent 2/3. Independently integrated the corner terms and limiting regular-polygon/rhombus trends; numerical finite epsilon checks are secondary.

Resultary nearest records concern short chords or boundary-point random hulls, not this area statistic.
